evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies two 1968 St. Louis Music Supply catalog advertisements for the Applied Fuzz and Treble Booster and treats early 1968 as the plausible start date. The article also documents Applied as an OEM builder for multiple branded versions.

Tone Machines identifies the Giulietti Fuzz and Treble Booster as an early version with the large battery lamp and On/Off control characteristic of the early Applied platform. Giulietti had a documented history of using outside manufacturers, including Hilgen, but no surviving model-specific factory document was found in this pass.

model_or_family: Applied Fuzz and Treble Booster candidate
evidence_summary: Tone Machines links the Scott-branded Applied-looking fuzz to Scott Music Supply Inc. of Louisiana after locating Scott's logo in a July 1968 Music Trades trade-show report. The physical pedal attribution remains a candidate because the surviving logo may be a later sticker or plate.

Effects Database identifies the Lou Rose Combo-Fuzz as a U.S.-made Applied Audio product and dates it around 1968. Tone Machines independently places Lou Rose units at the September 1968 opening of the Lou Rose Music Center in Edison, New Jersey.

Effects Database places Conrad Fuzzy Fury in the Applied Big Fuzz branch and provides a 1968 catalog reference. Tone Machines identifies the Conrad Fuzzy Fury, Bass Hawk and Sky Hawk as Applied-built Conrad effects released through David Wexler distribution, with the 1969 and 1970 catalogs listing the Sky Hawk.

Tone Machines identifies the Conrad Bass Hawk as part of the 1969 Conrad effects set built by Applied Audio. The exact surviving-product chronology is not fully pinned down, so the catalog window is kept qualified.

model_or_family: Sky Hawk - Fuzz and Treble Booster
evidence_summary: Tone Machines identifies Sky Hawk as a Conrad effect built by Applied Audio and notes it appears in both 1969 and 1970 catalogs even though physical examples are not known to the researcher. Keep as catalog-supported, specimen-light evidence.

model_or_family: Fuzzy Fury / Applied Big Fuzz relationship
evidence_summary: Effects Database groups Conrad Fuzzy Fury with Applied Big Fuzz and Goya Fury Box. This supports a shared Applied product branch but does not by itself establish that every related marketed state had identical production dates or construction.

physical_builder_candidate: Applied Audio Products Inc. and Trans-Tek Manufacturing Co.
evidence_summary: Tone Machines reports a June 1968 factory announcement for a new Trans-Tek plant in South Plainfield, New Jersey that would house Trans-Tek and Applied Audio as an associate organization, with workers building amplifiers and effects including Applied Big Fuzz. This is a facility/organizational relationship, not proof that Trans-Tek itself physically assembled every Applied pedal.
